## Goal

Notebook 04 learned two networks with MIIC, one per age class, with the same 25 L–R pairs (27 gene–gene links) and the
same settings:

| | Fetal (7–17 PCW) | Postnatal (3 months – 35 years) |
|---|---|---|
| Senders | CD8αα(I) 1,000 cells, 14 donors | CD8αα(I) 1,000 cells, 8 donors |
| Receivers | DC1 300 + aDC1 100 | DC1 300 + aDC1 35 |
| Metadata | senders: donor, chemistry, depth · receivers: population, donor, chemistry, depth | same |

Thymus case 2 pooled NK and CD8αα(I) senders and all ages. There, XCL1 depended only on XCL2 and on the NK / CD8αα(I)
label, and the drop of XCL1 at birth in CD8αα(I) cells (29% → 12% of cells, notebook 01) did not show in the network.
Here the claim of Park *et al.* is read with **CD8αα(I) cells only** as senders, the cell type it names:

> "GNG4⁺CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells expressed XCL1, which may be involved in the recruitment of XCR1-expressing DC1 cells. […]
> XCL1 is expressed most highly by CD8αα⁺ T(I) cells […] where these cells are activated and up-regulate CCR7."

Questions:

1. Within CD8αα(I) cells, what does XCL1 depend on, and is it the same before and after birth (section 2)?
2. On the receiver side, is the XCR1 / CCR7 picture of case 2 found in both age classes (section 3)?
3. Which other L–R links have a learned context, and does it change with age (section 4)?
4. How similar are the two networks, and what do depth and donor do in each (sections 1, 5 and 6)?

The networks are read as in case 2 (notebook 05): within each group a link means that two variables stay dependent
whatever other variable of the group is conditioned on; the L–R links between the groups are given, not learned.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

root <- getwd()
while (!file.exists(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))) {
  if (dirname(root) == root) stop("Repository root not found.")
  root <- dirname(root)
}
# link_name(), neighbors_of(), graph_distance(), column_cell_type(), network_data(), plot_network_*()
source(file.path(root, "scripts", "helpers.R"))

res_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "thymus_case3_xcl1_age")
out_dir <- file.path(res_dir, "05_interpretation")
fig_dir <- file.path(root, "results", "figures", "thymus_case3_xcl1_age")
dir.create(out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(fig_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

RUNS <- c("fetal", "postnatal")
SEND <- "CD8αα(I)"
RECV <- "DC1/aDC1"
META <- c("population", "donor", "method", "n_counts")

read_run <- function(run) {
  dir    <- file.path(res_dir, "04_causalccc", run)
  result <- readRDS(file.path(dir, "miic_input", "miic_result.rds"))
  mosaic <- read_csv(file.path(dir, "causalccc_files", "causalCCC_df.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE, guess_max = Inf)
  lr     <- read_tsv(file.path(dir, "causalccc_files", "causalCCC_interactEdges.tsv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  # Cell type of each variable: the group whose rows hold its values
  row_type <- if_else(!is.na(mosaic$donor_senders), SEND, RECV)
  type_of  <- column_cell_type(mosaic, row_type)
  lr_links <- link_name(lr$ligands, lr$receptors)
  # One row per pair of variables (MIIC lists each given L-R link twice, once per direction)
  edges <- result$all.edges.summary |>
    filter(type == "P") |>
    distinct(pair_a = pmin(x, y), pair_b = pmax(x, y), .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(-pair_a, -pair_b) |>
    mutate(is_lr = link_name(x, y) %in% lr_links,
           where = case_when(is_lr ~ "L–R (given)", type_of[x] == SEND ~ "within senders", .default = "within receivers"))
  list(run = run, result = result, mosaic = mosaic, lr = lr, lr_links = lr_links, row_type = row_type,
       type_of = type_of, edges = edges, intra = filter(edges, !is_lr))
}
nets <- set_names(map(RUNS, read_run), RUNS)

# Labels for the tables and drawings: no group suffix, metadata in brackets
var_label <- function(v) {
  label <- str_remove(v, "_(senders|receivers)$")
  if_else(label %in% META, paste0("[", label, "]"), label)
}
degree_of <- function(net, v) map_int(v, \(g) sum(net$intra$x == g | net$intra$y == g))
neighbour_string <- function(net, v, n = Inf) {
  nb <- net$intra |> filter(x == v | y == v) |>
    transmute(other = if_else(x == v, y, x), info_shifted) |> arrange(desc(info_shifted)) |> head(n)
  if (nrow(nb) == 0) return("–")
  paste0(var_label(nb$other), " (", round(nb$info_shifted), ")", collapse = ", ")
}
map_chr(nets, \(n) format(attr(n$result, "run_time")))
```

## 1. Overview of the two networks

```{r}
#| label: overview

map(nets, \(n) {
  vars <- tibble(variable = names(n$mosaic), group = n$type_of[names(n$mosaic)],
                 kind = if_else(str_remove(names(n$mosaic), "_(senders|receivers)$") %in% META, "metadata", "gene"))
  linked <- unique(c(n$edges$x, n$edges$y))
  vars |> group_by(where = if_else(group == SEND, "within senders", "within receivers")) |>
    summarise(genes = sum(kind == "gene"), metadata = sum(kind == "metadata"),
              variables_linked = sum(variable %in% linked)) |>
    left_join(n$edges |> group_by(where) |>
                summarise(links = n(), oriented = sum(abs(infOrt) == 2), genuine_causations = sum(is_causal == "Y")),
              by = "where")
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |> arrange(desc(where), run)
```

**Hubs**: the variables with the most learned links in each group and run.

```{r}
#| label: hubs

map(nets, \(n) {
  tibble(variable = unique(c(n$intra$x, n$intra$y))) |>
    mutate(group = n$type_of[variable], degree = degree_of(n, variable)) |>
    group_by(group) |> slice_max(degree, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE) |>
    mutate(rank = row_number(), label = paste0(var_label(variable), " (", degree, ")")) |>
    ungroup() |> select(group, rank, label)
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = c(group, run), values_from = label, names_sep = " · ")
```

**How similar are the two networks?** The gene selection was made separately in each run, so the networks share only
part of their variables. Among the links whose two variables are in both networks, how many are found in both?

```{r}
#| label: similarity

map(c("within senders", "within receivers"), \(w) {
  a <- nets$fetal$intra |> filter(where == w)
  b <- nets$postnatal$intra |> filter(where == w)
  shared_vars <- intersect(names(nets$fetal$mosaic)[nets$fetal$type_of == if_else(w == "within senders", SEND, RECV)],
                           names(nets$postnatal$mosaic)[nets$postnatal$type_of == if_else(w == "within senders", SEND, RECV)])
  la <- link_name(a$x, a$y)[a$x %in% shared_vars & a$y %in% shared_vars]
  lb <- link_name(b$x, b$y)[b$x %in% shared_vars & b$y %in% shared_vars]
  tibble(where = w, shared_variables = length(shared_vars), links_fetal = length(la), links_postnatal = length(lb),
         in_both = length(intersect(la, lb)), jaccard = round(length(intersect(la, lb)) / length(union(la, lb)), 2))
}) |> list_rbind()
```

**Reading.**
- **Run times:** the postnatal MIIC run took 19.5 minutes. The 1.4 days of the fetal run include a suspension of the
  computer (sleep) during the run; its computing time was of the same order.
- **Sizes:** both networks have about 140 genes per group.
  - Fetal: 307 links among the senders and 251 among the receivers, with 10 genuine causations.
  - Postnatal: 284 and 340 links, with 2 genuine causations.
- **Hubs:**
  - Sequencing depth `[n_counts]` is the first hub of every group (fetal 78 and 34 links; postnatal 58 and 42).
  - Among the senders it is followed by housekeeping and metabolic genes (EEF1A1, PPIA, GAPDH, PARK7, MIF).
  - In the postnatal senders, `[method]` (19 links) and **XCL1 (9 links)** are also hubs.
- **The two networks differ a lot:**
  - The gene selection was made separately in each run, so only 61 sender variables and 84 receiver variables are
    common to both.
  - Among the links between these common variables, few are found in both runs (Jaccard index 0.31 among the senders,
    0.22 among the receivers).
  - Comparisons between the runs are therefore made gene by gene, on the genes of the claim.

## 2. Senders: what XCL1 depends on, before and after birth

```{r}
#| label: xcl-neighbours

expand_grid(run = RUNS, variable = c("XCL1", "XCL2")) |>
  mutate(degree = map2_int(run, variable, \(r, v) degree_of(nets[[r]], v)),
         neighbours = map2_chr(run, variable, \(r, v) neighbour_string(nets[[r]], v))) |>
  arrange(variable, run)
```

```{r}
#| label: xcl-by-donor

# XCL1 and XCL2 in the sender cells of each run, per donor (raw counts of the mosaic table)
map(nets, \(n) {
  n$mosaic |> filter(n$row_type == SEND) |>
    group_by(donor = donor_senders) |>
    summarise(cells = n(), XCL1_detected = mean(XCL1 > 0), XCL1_mean = mean(XCL1), XCL2_detected = mean(XCL2 > 0),
              median_depth = median(n_counts_senders), .groups = "drop")
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |>
  filter(cells >= 20) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(v) round(v, 2)))
```

```{r}
#| label: xcl-coexpression

# XCL1 among XCL2+ and XCL2- cells, and distance from XCL1 to the design variables
map(nets, \(n) {
  s <- n$mosaic |> filter(n$row_type == SEND)
  d <- graph_distance(n$intra |> filter(where == "within senders"), "XCL1")
  tibble(cells = nrow(s), XCL1_detected = mean(s$XCL1 > 0),
         `XCL1+ among XCL2+` = mean(s$XCL1[s$XCL2 > 0] > 0), `XCL1+ among XCL2-` = mean(s$XCL1[s$XCL2 == 0] > 0),
         links_to_donor = d["donor_senders"], links_to_chemistry = d["method_senders"], links_to_depth = d["n_counts_senders"])
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |>
  mutate(across(where(is.double), \(v) round(v, 2)))
```

**Reading.**
- **XCL1 is linked to TNFRSF9 (4-1BB / CD137) in both age classes:** it is the strongest XCL1 neighbour in fetal cells
  (252, before XCL2, 221) and the second in postnatal cells (109).
  - TNFRSF9 is induced in T cells by TCR signalling.
  - Its other neighbours point to the same activation program: BIRC3, DUSP4 and MEF2C in fetal cells, BHLHE40 and RGS16
    (two genes induced by TCR signalling) in postnatal cells.
  - CRTAM, the other XCL-associated ligand, is linked to XCL1 in fetal cells and to BHLHE40 and RGS16 in postnatal cells.
  - **Within CD8αα(I) cells, XCL1 is therefore part of an activation program.** This was hidden in case 2, where NK
    cells dominated the XCL1 signal.
- **XCL2 goes with XCL1 at both ages:** 96% (fetal) and 92% (postnatal) of XCL2⁺ cells express XCL1, against 16% and
  8% of XCL2⁻ cells.
- **The design variables are not direct neighbours of XCL1** in either run (donor, chemistry, depth). Postnatally,
  XCL1 also links to PARK7, MAOB and MEST, metabolic genes whose meaning here is unclear.
- **The drop at birth is not a depth artefact:**
  - Postnatal cells are shallower (median 2,500–3,100 counts per donor, against 4,000–7,700 in fetal donors).
  - But XCL1 falls much more than depth: from 9–28 mean counts per fetal donor to 0.6–4.4 per postnatal donor.
  - On the normalised scale, the drop is about threefold (notebook 01).
- **GNG4 was not selected** in either network, so the "GNG4⁺" part of the claim rests on co-expression only
  (notebook 01: 59% of fetal GNG4⁺ CD8αα(I) cells express XCL1).

## 3. Receivers: XCR1, CCR7 and the activation of DC1

```{r}
#| label: receiver-neighbours

expand_grid(variable = c("XCR1", "CCR7", "LAMP3", "CD40", "CD80", "population"), run = RUNS) |>
  mutate(degree = map2_int(run, variable, \(r, v) degree_of(nets[[r]], v)),
         neighbours = map2_chr(run, variable, \(r, v) neighbour_string(nets[[r]], v)))
```

```{r}
#| label: receiver-distances

map(nets, \(n) {
  d <- graph_distance(n$intra |> filter(where == "within receivers"), "XCR1")
  tibble(to = c("population", "CCR7", "LAMP3", "CD40", "CD80", "IL12B"), links_from_XCR1 = unname(d[to]))
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = links_from_XCR1)
```

```{r}
#| label: xcr1-ccr7

map(nets, \(n) {
  n$mosaic |> filter(n$row_type == RECV) |>
    mutate(XCR1 = if_else(XCR1 > 0, "XCR1+", "XCR1-"), CCR7 = if_else(CCR7 > 0, "CCR7+", "CCR7-")) |>
    count(population, XCR1, CCR7) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = c(XCR1, CCR7), values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run")
```

**Reading.**
- **XCR1 has only DC1 neighbours:** FGL2 in both runs, and HLA-DQA1 postnatally. Unlike case 2, it is not directly
  linked to `[population]`: that link was weak in case 2 (16) and is lost with 300 DC1 instead of 500.
- **CCR7 and LAMP3 stay tied to the DC1 / aDC1 label at both ages:** 155 and 142 in fetal cells, 60 and 63 in
  postnatal cells. The links are weaker postnatally because there are only 35 aDC1.
- **The activation program around LAMP3 differs with age.** In fetal cells, LAMP3 is linked to CD40 and CD80 (as in
  case 2); in postnatal cells it is not. There, CD40 is linked to BCL2A1 and MARCKSL1 instead.
- **XCR1 and CCR7 remain almost mutually exclusive:**
  - fetal: 172 of 300 DC1 express XCR1 and 11 express CCR7; 90 of 100 aDC1 express CCR7 and 2 express XCR1;
  - postnatal: 146 of 300 DC1 express XCR1 and 18 express CCR7; 31 of 35 aDC1 express CCR7 and 1 expresses XCR1.
- **Conclusion for the receivers:** the picture of case 2 holds at both ages. XCR1 marks resting DC1, CCR7 and LAMP3
  mark activated DC1, and the activation genes do not depend on XCR1.

## 4. The L–R links, fetal and postnatal

For every given link, the learned context of the ligand (in CD8αα(I) cells) and of the receptor (in DC1 / aDC1 cells)
in each run. On the receiver side, a receptor linked to `[population]` is specific to DC1 or to aDC1. On the sender
side there is no population variable (one population): a ligand linked only to `[donor]`, `[method]` or `[n_counts]`
varies for technical or donor reasons; a ligand with gene neighbours belongs to a program of the cell.

```{r}
#| label: lr-table

lr_context <- map(nets, \(n) {
  n$lr |>
    mutate(ligand = var_label(ligands), receptor = var_label(receptors),
           ligand_degree = degree_of(n, ligands), receptor_degree = degree_of(n, receptors),
           receptor_to_population = map_lgl(receptors, \(g) "population" %in% neighbors_of(g, n$intra)$neighbor),
           ligand_neighbours = map_chr(ligands, \(g) neighbour_string(n, g, n = 3)),
           receptor_neighbours = map_chr(receptors, \(g) neighbour_string(n, g, n = 3)))
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run")

lr_context |>
  select(run, ligand, receptor, ligand_degree, ligand_neighbours) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = c(ligand_degree, ligand_neighbours)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
#| label: lr-receptors

lr_context |>
  distinct(run, receptor, receptor_degree, receptor_to_population, receptor_neighbours) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = c(receptor_degree, receptor_to_population, receptor_neighbours)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r}
#| label: lr-ligand-classes

# Context of each ligand gene: isolated, design variables only, or with genes
lr_context |>
  distinct(run, ligands, ligand) |>
  mutate(context = map2_chr(run, ligands, \(r, g) {
    nb <- neighbors_of(g, nets[[r]]$intra)$neighbor
    case_when(length(nb) == 0 ~ "isolated",
              all(str_remove(nb, "_(senders|receivers)$") %in% META) ~ "design variables only",
              .default = "with genes")
  })) |>
  count(run, context) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = run, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

**Reading.**
- **Almost every ligand has gene neighbours** (fetal 22 of 22, postnatal 20 of 22). The two postnatal exceptions,
  CD28 and ICAM3, are linked only to `[n_counts]`.
- **T-cell costimulation is a fetal feature here:**
  - In fetal cells, CD28 is linked to PDCD1, and its receptors CD80 and CD40 (ligand CD40LG) are next to LAMP3 on the
    aDC1 side, as in case 2.
  - In postnatal cells, CD28 depends only on depth, and CD40 / CD80 have left the LAMP3 module.
  - CD274 (PD-L1) is tied to the aDC1 label at both ages; PDCD1LG2 (PD-L2) only in fetal cells.
- **Other changes with age:**
  - CRTAM joins the TCR-activation genes postnatally (BHLHE40, RGS16).
  - CADM1 is linked to CLEC9A (DC1 identity) in fetal cells, to HLA-DPA1 in postnatal cells.
  - CD6 moves from XCL1 / ARHGDIB (fetal) to the T-cell identity genes CD5 and LEF1 (postnatal).
  - ITGA4 is tied to `[donor]` postnatally (112).
- **Ubiquitous pairs:** MIF → CD74 stays in the housekeeping (PPIA, GAPDH, NME2) and MHC class II modules at both
  ages, as in cases 1 and 2.

## 5. Design variables and sequencing depth

```{r}
#| label: meta-neighbours

expand_grid(run = RUNS, variable = c("donor_senders", "method_senders", "n_counts_senders",
                                     "population", "donor_receivers", "method_receivers", "n_counts_receivers")) |>
  mutate(degree = map2_int(run, variable, \(r, v) degree_of(nets[[r]], v)),
         neighbours = map2_chr(run, variable, \(r, v) neighbour_string(nets[[r]], v, n = 8)))
```

Genes that follow depth, measured as in case 2 (Spearman correlation with the total counts of the cell within each
population, median over the populations of the group, threshold 0.5), and the share of gene–gene links joining two of
them.

```{r}
#| label: depth-module

map(nets, \(n) {
  gene_vars <- names(n$mosaic)[!str_remove(names(n$mosaic), "_(senders|receivers)$") %in% META]
  pop <- if_else(n$row_type == SEND, "CD8αα(I)", n$mosaic$population)
  depth <- coalesce(n$mosaic$n_counts_senders, n$mosaic$n_counts_receivers)
  rho <- map_dbl(gene_vars, \(v) {
    rows <- n$row_type == n$type_of[[v]]
    x <- n$mosaic[[v]][rows]
    r <- tapply(seq_along(x), pop[rows], \(i) if (sd(x[i]) == 0) NA_real_ else cor(x[i], depth[rows][i], method = "spearman"))
    median(unlist(r), na.rm = TRUE)
  }) |> set_names(gene_vars)
  follows <- gene_vars[!is.na(rho) & rho > 0.5]
  n$intra |> filter(x %in% gene_vars, y %in% gene_vars) |>
    group_by(where) |>
    summarise(gene_gene_links = n(), both_follow_depth = sum(x %in% follows & y %in% follows)) |>
    mutate(share = both_follow_depth / gene_gene_links,
           expected_by_chance = map_dbl(where, \(w) {
             g <- gene_vars[n$type_of[gene_vars] == if_else(w == "within senders", SEND, RECV)]
             mean(g %in% follows)^2
           }))
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run") |>
  mutate(across(c(share, expected_by_chance), \(v) round(v, 3)))
```

**Reading.**
- **Depth structures both networks.**
  - In fetal sender cells, most selected genes follow depth: 59% of gene–gene links join two depth-following genes,
    against 43% by chance.
  - In postnatal sender cells, the share is 17% against 4%.
  - Among the receivers, it is 71% and 73% (51% and 56% by chance), as in case 2.
- **Postnatally, chemistry and donor are confounded among the senders.** `[method]`–`[donor]` is the strongest link
  (562), and `[method]` has 19 links. The postnatal donors were sequenced either 3′ (P1–P3) or 5′ (T03, T06, T07,
  A43), with A16 in both, so a chemistry effect cannot be told apart from a donor effect.
- **Fetal donor** links only to a handful of genes (HLA-DRB5 and housekeeping genes), as in case 2.
- **None of the claim's genes is directly linked to donor, chemistry or depth** in either run.

## 6. Orientations and genuine causations

```{r}
#| label: orientations

oriented <- map(nets, \(n) {
  n$edges |>
    filter(abs(infOrt) == 2) |>
    transmute(from = if_else(infOrt == 2, x, y), to = if_else(infOrt == 2, y, x), where,
              strength = round(info_shifted), genuine = is_causal,
              involves_metadata = str_detect(paste(from, to), "(population|donor|method|n_counts)"))
}) |> list_rbind(names_to = "run")
oriented |> count(run, where, involves_metadata, genuine)
```

```{r}
#| label: genuine

oriented |>
  filter(genuine == "Y" | str_detect(paste(from, to), "XCL|XCR1|CCR7|LAMP3")) |>
  mutate(from = var_label(from), to = var_label(to)) |>
  arrange(run, desc(genuine), desc(strength)) |>
  as.data.frame()
```

**Reading.**
- **Fetal: 50 links are oriented, and 10 are genuine causations.**
  - 7 go from `[n_counts]` to housekeeping genes (UBA52, SUMO2, TMSB10, SLC25A5, EIF3K, GNG5, PHB2): depth as a cause
    of counts, the expected technical direction.
  - The other 3 are ATP5E → FAU, CPVL → LYZ and CPVL → CORO1A.
- **Postnatal: 33 links are oriented, and 2 are genuine causations,** `[method]` → PCBP2 and `[n_counts]` → RAN, both
  technical.
- **No orientation involves XCL1, XCL2, XCR1 or CCR7** in either run.

## 7. The networks, drawn

Same conventions as case 2: colours are the two groups; diamonds are the centres (XCL1, XCL2, XCR1); dashed lines are
the given L–R links (drawn thin); an arrowhead is an orientation found by MIIC, and a green link a genuine causation;
thicker links are stronger. Metadata variables are in brackets.

```{r}
#| label: drawing-setup

# Colours of the two groups for the drawing functions of scripts/helpers.R (which read these two global vectors)
cell_type_colours <- set_names(c("#f2c57c", "#9cc3e6"), c(SEND, RECV))
cell_type_borders <- set_names(c("#a8742a", "#2f6491"), c(SEND, RECV))
centres <- c("XCL1", "XCL2", "XCR1")
claim_nets <- map(nets, \(n) network_data(n$edges, n$lr_links, n$type_of, var_label, centres = centres, max_distance = 2))
map(claim_nets, \(cn) c(variables = nrow(cn$nodes), links = nrow(cn$links))) |> bind_rows(.id = "run")
```

                               label_size = 2.8)
ggsave(file.path(fig_dir, "05_claim_neighbourhood_fetal.png"), p_fetal, width = 11, height = 9, dpi = 200)
p_fetal

### The neighbourhood of the claim, postnatal

## Conclusions

1. **XCL1 in CD8αα(I) cells drops at birth.**
   - 29% of fetal against 12% of postnatal cells express it (notebook 01).
   - The drop is much larger than the difference in sequencing depth.
   - Before and after birth, XCL1 belongs to an activation program of these cells: it is linked to TNFRSF9 (4-1BB) in
     both runs, with BIRC3 and DUSP4 (fetal) or BHLHE40 and RGS16 (postnatal) nearby, and goes with XCL2 and CRTAM.
   - So the XCL1 source in CD8αα(I) cells is their activated (4-1BB⁺) fraction, which is larger before birth. This
     refines the claim: CD8αα(I) cells are an XCL1 source mainly in the fetal thymus, and it is the cells carrying a
     TCR-activation signature that produce it.
   - GNG4 is not in the networks, so its role cannot be read from them.
2. **The receiver side is the same at both ages, and as in case 2.**
   - XCR1 marks resting DC1, and CCR7 / LAMP3 mark activated DC1; the two are almost never co-expressed.
   - The activation program does not depend on XCR1.
   - The claim's "activated […] up-regulate CCR7" is a change of state that the networks describe but cannot attribute
     to XCL1 signalling.
3. **Costimulation is a fetal feature in these networks.** CD28 → CD80, CD40LG → CD40 and PDCD1 → CD274 connect
   CD8αα(I) cells to the aDC1 activation module in fetal cells; postnatally only PD-L1 stays tied to aDC1, with 35 aDC1
   cells only.

**Limits.**
- The two networks rest on different gene selections and share few links (Jaccard 0.22–0.31), so they are compared
  gene by gene.
- Postnatal aDC1 has only 35 cells.
- Postnatally, chemistry and donor are confounded.
- As in cases 1 and 2, the L–R links are given, not inferred, and the orientations involving the claim's genes are
  not causal.

**Possible next steps.**
- Split CD8αα(I) cells into TNFRSF9⁺ and TNFRSF9⁻ and compare their XCL1, XCL2 and GNG4 expression.
- Check whether the TNFRSF9⁺ XCL1⁺ CD8αα(I) cells match the authors' "T(agonist)" population.

**Outputs:**
- `results/thymus_case3_xcl1_age/05_interpretation/retained_links.csv`: every link of both runs;
- `results/thymus_case3_xcl1_age/05_interpretation/lr_links_context.csv`: the context of each L–R link per run;
- `results/figures/thymus_case3_xcl1_age/05_claim_neighbourhood_fetal.png` and `..._postnatal.png`: the static figures.
